evals.prompt: Show me my in-progress Linear issues as a small table with id, status, priority, and title.
evals.expected_output: Uses linear issue list with assignee me and a started/In Progress state filter, uses --fields to limit output, pipes JSON to jq or formats it into a table, and explains the result.
assertions: Output includes a linear issue list command
Command filters assignee to the current user with -a me
Command filters to started/In Progress state
Command uses --fields or jq to select id/status/priority/title
Response presents the results as a readable table or list

evals.prompt: Create a bug in the Engineering team titled 'Checkout page hangs on coupon apply'. Body: Steps: open checkout, enter SAVE10, click Apply. Expected: discount appears. Actual: spinner never stops. Priority high, labels checkout and regression.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this as a write, shows a linear issue create command with -t Engineering, the title, a multi-line Markdown body via --body-file or -b with real newlines, --priority high and --labels checkout,regression, and asks for confirmation before running unless told to run now.
assertions: Output treats issue creation as a write operation requiring confirmation
Command uses linear issue create with -t Engineering and the requested title
Command sets --priority high and --labels with both labels
Command preserves the multiline body accurately (body-file or literal newlines)
Response notes --labels replaces the full label set only on update, or otherwise handles labels correctly

evals.prompt: Append a '## Rollout plan' section to the description of issue ENG-123 in Linear without touching the rest of the description.
evals.expected_output: Uses the patch mechanism via linear call save_issue with an append (or insert_after) op rather than rewriting the whole description with -b.
assertions: Output does not rewrite the full description with -b/--body-file
Command uses linear call save_issue with a patch array
Patch uses append or an anchor-based insert op

evals.prompt: Which Linear MCP tools deal with releases, and how would I list release pipelines from the shell?
evals.expected_output: Uses linear tools release (or the tools.md catalog) for discovery and shows linear call list_release_pipelines, mentioning mcpc @linear tools-get for schemas.
assertions: Output uses linear tools or the catalog reference for discovery
Output shows a linear call list_release_pipelines command
Output mentions checking the tool schema before raw calls
